newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African nurse dies from deadly Ebola fever.
newsitem.headline: S.African nurse dies from deadly Ebola fever.

text.p: A South African nurse who caught the deadly Ebola fever from a patient died of the disease on Sunday night, health officials said.
Marilyn Lahana, a 46-year-old mother of two who nursed a Gabonese doctor and contracted Ebola from him, died after suffering severe brain damage during a haemorrhage.
She was also suffering from multiple organ dysfunction caused by the disease, which she caught from the doctor she had treated for an unrelated disorder at the end of October.
The doctor has since recovered and returned home.
Ebola, which killed 245 people in Zaire last year and 35 people in two outbreaks in Gabon earlier this year, is fatal in 80 to 90 percent of cases.
With early diagnosis, the fatality rate can be lowered to around 30 percent.

World Health Organisation (WHO) doctor Brian Gushulak arrived in South Africa on Sunday to study Lahana's case, as well as those of around 300 people who might have had contact with her or the Gabonese doctor.
